q1.title: Which kind of topic naturally pulls you in?
q1.a: Understanding how software, automation or data systems work
q1.b: Figuring out how machines, structures or physical systems work
q1.c: Exploring living systems, ecosystems and the natural world
q1.d: Examining people, culture, history and ideas

q2.title: When solving a problem, what kind of thinking feels most natural?
q2.a: Breaking things into clear steps, patterns or logic
q2.b: Testing ideas hands-on until something works
q2.c: Observing, researching and testing with evidence
q2.d: Interpreting meaning through language, ideas or philosophy

q3.title: Which kind of environment would energize you most?
q3.a: A fast-moving setting focused on strategy, leadership or innovation
q3.b: A learning environment where people grow through teaching or mentoring
q3.c: A care-focused setting centered on helping others
q3.d: A creative space for design, expression or artistic work

q4.title: Which kind of task could you happily spend hours on?
q4.a: Building or improving digital tools, systems or workflows
q4.b: Designing or improving physical objects or systems
q4.c: Creating visual, written or expressive creative work
q4.d: Studying people, groups or societies to find patterns

q5.title: Which kind of challenge feels motivating rather than draining?
q5.a: Turning ideas into products, plans or organizations
q5.b: Teaching, explaining or helping others understand
q5.c: Improving health, well-being or quality of life
q5.d: Creating something original through art, design or storytelling

q6.title: If you were leading a project, which role would you naturally take?
q6.a: Researching, testing ideas and working with data
q6.b: Communicating ideas through writing, speaking or storytelling
q6.d: Advocating for people, policy or social change

q7.title: If your work made a difference, what kind of impact would matter most to you?
q7.a: Helping people learn, grow or access education
q7.b: Improving health and wellness, or reducing suffering
q7.c: Deepening understanding of culture, ethics or ideas
q7.d: Making society fairer through systems, policy or community action

q8.title: Which sounds most like you right now?
q8.aText: I want to build the brain of the app: elegant code, secure data, systems that never break.
q8.bText: I want to investigate how the natural world works through observation and experiments.
q8.cText: I want to build organizations, make decisions and create value in the world.

q9.title: Which first project would you be most excited to start?
q9.a: Studying cells, molecules or how a disease spreads
q9.b: Designing a bridge, a machine or a better building
q9.c: Training a model or analyzing a large data set
q9.d: Researching how a community, market or government decision works

q10.title: Which of these would you most like to be known for?
q10.a: Helping people stay healthy and understand themselves
q10.b: Building and leading a successful venture
q10.c: Creating work that people see, read or hear
q10.d: Solving a hard problem with numbers and theory

allDone.text: Every step is done. Keep an eye on the deadlines and the answers from universities below.

countries.title: Choose where you want to study
countries.why: Countries differ in cost, exams and deadlines, so everything else depends on this choice.
countries.s1: Open the short setup and answer the questions about countries.
countries.s2: Pick up to three countries: you can change them at any time.
countries.s3: Save: tests, deadlines and universities will adjust to your choice.

major.title: Choose what you want to study
major.why: Universities admit to a field of study, and your activities and essays should point to it.
major.s1: Not sure yet? Take the short interests quiz in “Profile” first.
major.s2: Open the setup and pick one or two fields.
major.s3: Save: universities and ideas will be matched to these fields.

activities.title: Describe what you do outside lessons
activities.why: Admission officers read your activities right after your grades: they show who you are.
activities.s1: Add one activity: a club, a project, a competition, volunteering, a job.
activities.s2: Write what exactly you did and what came out of it, with numbers.
activities.s3: Mark it as ready and add the next one until you reach the goal.

tests.title: Plan and take your tests
tests.why: Most universities abroad ask for a language test, and many ask for the SAT or a similar exam.
tests.s1: See which tests your countries and universities ask for.
tests.s2: Choose a date and add the test to your plan.
tests.s3: When the result arrives, enter your score here.

list.title: Build your list of universities
list.why: A balanced list has ambitious, realistic and safe options, so you get at least one offer.
list.s1: Open the university search: it already knows your countries and field.
list.s2: Compare cost, requirements and your chances.
list.s3: Add universities to your list until you reach the goal.

statement.title: Write your main essay
statement.why: It is the one place where universities hear your own voice, and it goes to almost all of them.
statement.s1: Choose a story only you can tell.
statement.s2: Write a first draft: it does not have to be good yet.
statement.s3: Read the feedback, rewrite, and mark the essay as final.

supplements.title: Write the essays for each university
supplements.why: Many universities ask their own short questions, usually about why you chose them.
supplements.s1: Open the list of questions for your universities.
supplements.s3: Mark each essay as final when it is ready.

documents.title: Collect your documents
documents.why: Transcripts, recommendations and certificates take weeks to prepare, so start early.
documents.s1: Open the checklist: it shows only what your universities need.
documents.s2: Ask teachers for recommendations at least a month ahead.
documents.s3: Tick each document when it is ready.

apply.title: Send your applications
apply.why: Everything is ready. What is left is to submit on time on each university's site.
apply.s1: Open your list and start with the nearest deadline.
apply.s2: Submit the application on the university's site and pay the fee if there is one.
apply.s3: Come back and mark the university as submitted.

results.title: Record the answers
results.why: With all the answers in one place it is easier to compare offers and scholarships.
results.s1: Check your email and the university accounts.
results.s2: Mark each answer in your list: accepted, waitlist or refused.
results.s3: Compare the offers and choose where you will go.
